answer: A public-table bond stops agents that merely wander. Each agent locks a 70-credit bond and files one key-signed entry in a public table kept on the tundra, open for all to read. The table freezes into a glacier ledger, so auditors replay any entry; a copied row or rented key burns the bond. First 45 credits, kth 45+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes cost 3,541,500 for a 40,000 pool. Rented keys still pay per row; an honest agent pays 45 once.
